$comment: Registry of every component forge installs. installed[] lists ways to detect it locally (first hit wins); latest says where the newest public version lives (never a pinned version); install/update are exact commands per platform (afterUpdate lists notes shown with an update command, as a list or per platform; a detector in installed[] may carry its own update, and requires, for a component found that way: pip, uv tool, pipx, a loose skill; a plain list holds on every platform; requires lists tools the commands need, as a list or per platform), printed by scripts/doctor.mjs and never run without the user's yes. Paths: ~ is the home dir, %VAR% an environment variable.

windows: $Dest = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA/ai-memory"; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $Dest | Out-Null; Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/releases/latest/download/ai-memory-windows-x86_64.zip" -OutFile "$env:TEMP/ai-memory.zip"; Expand-Archive "$env:TEMP/ai-memory.zip" -DestinationPath $Dest -Force; Get-ChildItem "$Dest/ai-memory.exe" | Unblock-File

windows: Restart the `ai-memory serve` process afterwards (the terminal, service or scheduled task that runs it): the MCP server is a separate process that keeps using the old binary until it restarts, and closing Claude Code does not stop it.

The running ai-memory.exe cannot be overwritten, so the old one is renamed to ai-memory.exe.old first (a previous .old is deleted); if the rename fails because that .old is still in use, stop the process that still runs ai-memory.exe.old (usually `ai-memory serve`) and run the command again.
